source.title: Artificial Supercavitation. Physics and Calculation
source.author: Vladimir N. Semenenko

definitions.xbar: physical downstream coordinate x / Rn, origin at disk plane
definitions.Lc: reported approximate total physical cavity length; not C1 disk-image separation by definition

source.evidence_kind: Primary author lecture; semiempirical correlations based partly on experiments; not raw measured samples and not an exact numerical solution

relations.validity: Closure/gas-leakage approximation for a cavity closing on an afterbody with Db<=Dc. No universal k2 is supplied. Not a cylinder surface-flow solution and not a basis for invented gas-leakage data.
Disk asymptotic relation as sigma tends to zero; not a finite-sigma exact result.
Small cavitation number and negligible gravity. For other blunt cavitators Dn means separation-line diameter. A about 2 when sigma is not very small; no universal exact A is supplied.
Approximate empirical drag correlation for blunt cavitators; disk coefficient about 0.82. No fit to the current BEM.
Blunt-cone approximation. This is not an arbitrary-cylinder coefficient.
Near-front disk-cavity approximation, independent of sigma; common join chosen at xbar=2 in source Eq32 and Eq52.
Semiempirical fit to natural vapor supercavities behind disks. Source Fig13 shows closure on an afterbody/nozzle jet. Root of the polynomial is not a separately verified physical closure condition.
Rounded correlation derived from Eq32; same source data range. Coefficient from literal Eq32 extremum is 0.847**2/(4*0.236) = 0.759967..., so the two are not algebraically identical.
Reported approximate length; not the positive zero of literal Eq32. Source plots Eq33/34 over sigma .01-.06, while profile-fit data range is .012-.057.

definitions.mu: radial fluid-layer logarithmic inertia parameter; approximately constant in slender-cavity main region

relations.validity: Section-expansion approximation. This does not supply arbitrary detached bubble dynamics or cylinder wetting by itself.

relations.ambiguity: The scanned primary prints no absolute-value bars around the fractional-power base. kappa=1 is unambiguous and is used by source Fig12. A general downstream kappa=.85 implementation needs a separately sourced absolute-value continuation; do not silently invent one.
relations.validity: Matched front/main approximate profile, not a model for the unsteady frothy tail. Distinct from the direct semiempirical polynomial Eq32.

relations.source: V.V. Serebriakov, Asymptotic Solution of the Problem for a Thin Axisymmetric Cavern; NASA translation of Dopovidi Akad. Nauk UkrSSR Ser.A No12 (1973),1120-1122
equations: X = x/lk; lk=lambda*Rk; origin at cavity middle
relations.validity: Two-term slender-axisymmetric-cavity asymptotic profile for constant sigma, large lambda. Main-region idealization, not the literal disk-front relation. Rk remains undetermined until separate drag relation is supplied. No exact finite-sigma or cylinder wetting claim.

visual_verification.review_table6_printed_error: The printed Logvinovich Rk relation omits a square root; primary Eq28 has sqrt(cx/(k*sigma)). Review table must not be used as code authority for that expression.

profile_sample_policy: Raw equation evaluations. Front and main join values both retained. Finite radius at independently reported Eq34 length is retained; a separately labelled algebraic continuation proceeds to just before the positive polynomial root. Root is recorded separately, never advertised as physical closure or substituted for Eq34 length.
cylinder_scope: Disk-headed dry cylindrical afterbody can be checked for containment in an explicit approximate cavity envelope. This does not solve wetted flow around an arbitrary cylinder or determine reattachment/gas leakage.
closure_distinction: Riabouchinsky artificial solid closer, Joukowski-Roshko cylinder at maximum cavity diameter, and Gilbarg-Efros closure on smaller cylinder with annular reentrant jet are separate primary schemes. A free detached bubble is another problem.
